title: Give glass and water their own IOR and Opacity defaults in the surface spec
body:
## Summary
Water dispatches IOR 1.5 (glass's value) and both glass and water dispatch Opacity 1 (fully opaque), because the surface spec only carries per-surface Roughness/Metallic.

## Description
src/lib/materials/surface-spec.ts:34 types `defaults` as { Roughness, Metallic } only, and src/components/modules/content/materials/MaterialParameterConfigurator/helpers.ts:16 copies just those two. Every other slider falls to the shared BASE_PARAMS default (src/components/modules/content/materials/MaterialParameterConfigurator/constants.ts:39-42): Opacity 1 and IOR 1.5 for both glass and water. The configurator's own copy at constants.ts:42 says "water ~ 1.33", and the only two surfaces that show Opacity start fully solid. shader-budget-authoring (surface-to-shading-model-map) asks for ONE stated mapping from surface to shading model AND property ranges, read by estimator, authoring surface and analyser alike. Fixed = SurfaceSpec.defaults grows optional per-surface values (water IOR 1.33, glass/water Opacity < 1), surfaceParamDefaults copies every key, and the IOR step admits 1.33 (step 0.01) or surfaceDefaultsOnGrid.test.ts goes red.

## Flow
- pick Water -> Generate -> prompt Parameter Defaults: "IOR: default=1.5", "Opacity: default=1"
- fix: extend SurfaceSpec.defaults (surface-spec.ts), copy all keys in helpers.ts surfaceParamDefaults, set IOR step 0.01
- prompt goldens use their own fixture config; expected unchanged

## Expected impact
Generated water/glass materials start translucent and with the right refraction instead of an opaque glass-IOR slab. Could break: any golden whose fixture relies on surface defaults.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the dispatched defaults match the physical surface the designer picked
Before: water IOR 1.5 (its own copy says 1.33); glass and water Opacity 1 - 3 of 4 surface-specific values wrong
After: predicted 0 of 4 (water IOR 1.33, Opacity < 1 on both)
Method: simulation - walked both surfaces through helpers.ts + handleGenerate; the seam (surface-spec.ts) is owned by blueprint-tools, so not built here
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a hook test that selects water and glass, calls handleGenerate, and asserts params.IOR.defaultValue 1.33 for water and params.Opacity.defaultValue < 1 for both (red today: 1.5 / 1 / 1)

title: Move the Patterns and Style tabs onto the CLITask rail
body:
## Summary
PatternsTab and StyleTransferTab dispatch hand-built prompts through cli.sendPrompt, while ConfiguratorTab and PostProcessTab go through TaskFactory + cli.execute.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/materials/tabs/ConfiguratorTab.tsx:16-20 states the rule: "Never sendPrompt with a hand-built prompt" - on the rail buildTaskPrompt composes the prompt, prompt-evolution can resolve a variant, an A/B can test it and the inspector previews the exact string. src/components/modules/content/materials/tabs/PatternsTab.tsx:22 and src/components/modules/content/materials/tabs/StyleTransferTab.tsx:22 call cli.sendPrompt(buildXPrompt(...)) and read projectName/projectPath/ueVersion themselves, so they skip the project scan, skills, variants and the task-type model-policy pin. Fixed = TaskFactory.materialPattern / .styleTransfer in src/lib/cli-task.ts with verbatim handlers (as postProcess did in 8545dbf2), both tabs calling cli.execute.

## Flow
- open Patterns -> Generate -> sendPrompt(prompt) with no taskType -> no variant, no model-policy pin
- fix: two TaskFactory entries + handlers in cli-task.ts, switch both tabs to execute, add a rail test like material-configurator-rail.test.ts

## Expected impact
Pattern and style generations become A/B-able and previewable like the rest of the module. Could break: prompt text if a handler is not verbatim (pin with a golden).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every Materials CLI dispatch rides the CLITask rail
Before: 2 of 4 prompt-dispatching Materials tabs off the rail (PatternsTab.tsx:22, StyleTransferTab.tsx:22)
After: predicted 0 of 4
Method: probe - counted sendPrompt vs execute call sites in tabs/; not built because the TaskFactory seam (src/lib/cli-task.ts) is outside this context and StyleTransfer belongs to material-style-tools
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a rail test per tab: mock useModuleCLI, click Generate, assert execute is called with a task whose buildTaskPrompt output equals the old hand-built prompt byte-for-byte and sendPrompt is not called

title: Show an unset parent scalar as unset, not as its minimum
body:
## Summary
A live parent's scalar with no numeric manifest default renders its slider and readout at the minimum, but that value never dispatches until the slider is moved.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/materials/MaterialParameterConfigurator/liveParent.ts:81 sets the ParamDef defaultValue to `s.defaultValue ?? s.min`; src/components/modules/content/materials/MaterialParameterConfigurator/ParametersSection.tsx:32 reads `paramValues[p.name] ?? p.defaultValue`, so readout and aria-valuetext say e.g. "0.00 of 0 to 1". src/components/modules/content/materials/MaterialParameterConfigurator/useMaterialParameterConfigurator.ts:86-88 then skips it (val === null -> continue). The designer sees a value the prompt will not carry; the instance keeps the parent's value. Fixed = the section knows a param is unset (a ParamDef `unset` flag) and reads "not overridden" until moved.

## Flow
- adopt a live master whose scalar Wetness has defaultValue "curve:Wet" -> slider reads 0.00
- Generate -> prompt: "Wetness (no numeric default in the manifest)", no default= line
- the readout claimed 0.00 would be used

## Expected impact
Designers stop believing an override exists that does not. Could break: parent tests that count rows or read their text.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the readout matches what will dispatch
Before: 1 of 1 null-default parent scalars reads a number (its min) that does not dispatch
After: predicted 0 of 1 (reads "not overridden")
Method: simulation - walked liveParent.test.ts's Wetness case through parentParamDefs -> ParametersSection -> handleGenerate; not built because the unset copy/visual is a UX choice with no repo precedent
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render MaterialParameterConfigurator with a mocked manifest master carrying a non-numeric scalar default, adopt it, assert its row reads "not overridden" (red today: "0.00")

title: Decide whether the Hierarchy graph should draw all six materials checklist items
body:
## Summary
The Hierarchy tab draws mat-1..mat-3 and reports "x/3 NODES_COMPILED", while the materials checklist declares six items.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/materials/MaterialLayerGraph.tsx:33-37 hard-codes three nodes; src/lib/module-registry.ts:716-718 declares mat-4 (environment material set), mat-5 (HLSL custom nodes), mat-6 (optimize performance). GRAPH_STATUS (MaterialLayerGraph.tsx:94) divides by nodeStates.length = 3, so a module with 3 of 6 items done reads "3/3 NODES_COMPILED". Whether mat-4..6 belong in the hierarchy (they build on mat-1/mat-2) or the status should say hierarchy-only is a product call.

## Flow
- complete mat-1..3 -> header reads 3/3 NODES_COMPILED while the checklist shows 3/6
- option A: add mat-4 (prereq mat-2), mat-5 and mat-6 (prereq mat-1) as tier-2 nodes; the connector currently draws exactly two drops and must become data-driven
- option B: keep three nodes, label the status as hierarchy-only

## Expected impact
The status line stops reading complete while half the checklist is open. Could break: the fixed two-drop connector layout (MaterialLayerGraph.tsx:121-128).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the graph's completion count is not mistaken for the module's
Before: denominator 3 vs checklist 6
After: 6 (option A) or an explicit hierarchy-only label (option B)
Method: probe - counted HIERARCHY entries vs getModuleChecklist('materials') ids
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
src/components/modules/content/materials/MaterialLayerGraph.tsx:33-37 HIERARCHY = [mat-1, mat-2, mat-3]
src/components/modules/content/materials/MaterialLayerGraph.tsx:94 GRAPH_STATUS: {completedCount}/{nodeStates.length} NODES_COMPILED
src/lib/module-registry.ts:713-718 mat-1..mat-6
instrument: operator picks A or B; then a render test asserting the denominator equals the chosen set
